title: Skill: revalidate-done-tasks — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #92 (skill-revalidate-done-tasks), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

decisions.decision: On re-review of PR #92 (fixing the two blocking findings from the prior needs_work round), checklist items 1 and 2 here were verified against the current `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` content and marked `done: true` — both are now textually present (step 4's `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` instruction; step 5's guidance to leave a reopened task's stale `review`/`pr_decision` fields untouched but call out the regression explicitly). This matches what the parent task's own `decisions` array already recorded (task-worker's 2026-09-17T18:14:30Z entry) and was independently confirmed by the `code-review` skill run as part of this re-review, which flagged the two items as stale-but-unmarked on this very file. Item 3 (shared-working-tree coordination caveat) was judged only partially resolved — SKILL.md's new step 0 substantially covers the core risk (an explicit git-status-based mid-flight guard) but doesn't extend CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time' rule to name this skill and doesn't catch an agent that's mid-flight without yet having an uncommitted diff — so it stays open, with its text updated to describe the residual gap rather than restate the now-resolved core concern. Two further non-blocking findings surfaced by this re-review's own `code-review` pass (same-day audit-branch name collision; a residual staleness window between step 0's checkout and the later branch cut, after the potentially long test-suite run) were added as new checklist items rather than left only in the PR review comment.
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule and this project's own review process exist precisely to avoid a checklist claiming open work that's already resolved (or, conversely, silently closing something only partially fixed) going unnoticed once a PR merges and the review comment disappears from view. Verifying directly against SKILL.md's current text (not trusting task-worker's or the code-review skill's self-report at face value) was necessary since the two sources characterized the third item differently ('substantially covered' vs. simply unaddressed) — reading the actual step 0 text was the only way to resolve that ambiguity, and it supports a middle judgment: real but partial mitigation, so the item stays open rather than being marked fully done or left describing a problem that no longer fully exists as originally worded.

decisions.decision: Closed all three remaining checklist items. Item 3 (coordination caveat) was resolved via both of its own suggested paths rather than picking only one, since the prior decision entry explicitly allowed closing on either: (a) extended CLAUDE.md's 'One agent at a time on the shared working tree' bullet to name `revalidate-done-tasks` explicitly and point at its own step 0 guard, and (b) strengthened SKILL.md's step 0 itself so a clean `git status` is no longer treated as sufficient — it now also checks whether the current `HEAD` branch (if not `main`) has an open PR via `gh pr view`/`gh pr list --head`, treating an open PR on a non-`main` checkout as a possible mid-flight signal even with a clean tree, and only proceeding past it once that PR is merged/closed or doesn't exist. This narrows but doesn't fully close the gap — an agent mid-flight directly on `main` (e.g. a concurrent invocation of this same skill) still isn't caught, which the updated step 0 text now says explicitly rather than implying full coverage. Item 4 (same-day branch collision): `audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>` cutting now first checks whether that branch name already exists; if it does and still carries an open PR, the run switches to it and adds its findings there instead of opening a duplicate; if the existing branch's PR is already merged/closed, the run falls back to a numeric-suffixed name (`-2`, `-3`, ...). Reusing the open-PR branch (rather than always suffixing) was chosen over always-suffix because a same-day rerun's findings genuinely belong in one coherent PR per the skill's existing 'one branch per run, not per task' rationale — two same-day PRs for the same kind of audit would fragment review for no benefit. Item 5 (staleness window): step 1 now re-fetches and re-confirms `main` against `origin/main` immediately before cutting the branch, pulling fast-forward if `main` moved during the (potentially multi-minute) suite run in step 3, and instructs noting in the PR body if that happened so a reader knows the audited commit vs. current `main` may differ slightly — rather than trying to re-run the whole audit against the newer commit, which would reintroduce the same expensive-full-rerun problem step 0's design rationale already argues against.
decisions.rationale: All three fixes are documentation-only changes to `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` — no application code or task-board mechanics needed to change, matching this task's `skill: null` scoping (general engineering judgment on the coordination/process docs the parent task's PR review already flagged, not indicator/API/frontend work with a dedicated skill of its own). Kept each fix minimal and consistent with the parent task's own decision log (e.g. not re-litigating the already-closed items 1 and 2, and treating the residual mid-flight gap as inherently partial rather than overclaiming a full mutex the shared-working-tree model doesn't actually provide).

decisions.decision: Fixed the item-4/item-5 composition bug flagged as PR #93's blocking review finding: in `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s 'Handling a task that no longer holds' step 1, the same-day-collision branch-reuse path (`git fetch origin <branch> && git switch <branch>` when an existing today-dated branch still has an open PR) now explicitly reconciles that reused branch with the freshly re-confirmed `main` from earlier in the same step, via `git merge origin/main` into the reused branch before adding the current run's findings on top — rather than leaving it silently based on whatever `main` an earlier same-day run started from. Chose `merge` over `rebase` for this reconciliation because the branch may already have an open PR with prior commits a reviewer has seen (or will see) on GitHub; a rebase would rewrite those commits' SHAs and force-push, which is a worse property for a PR a human is expected to just read and merge directly (per this skill's own step 7 description of it as a direct board-authoring PR) than a merge commit that preserves history. The updated text also instructs noting in the PR body update which commits the merge picked up, so a reader isn't misled into thinking the branch is still based on the original day-start `main`, and instructs stopping and reporting (not silently resolving) on the unlikely case of a merge conflict, consistent with this skill's read-only/report-don't-silently-fix posture elsewhere. Considered an alternative of always cutting a fresh numeric-suffixed branch instead of ever reusing an open-PR same-day branch (which would sidestep the reconciliation problem entirely by construction) but rejected it: it was the exact 'always-suffix' option the item-4 decision already explicitly considered and rejected in favor of one-coherent-PR-per-day, and reverting that choice now to dodge this bug would just trade a real staleness problem for the fragmented-review problem item 4 was written to avoid, rather than actually fixing the composition gap.
decisions.rationale: The review comment on PR #93 was explicit that item 5's checklist claim ('closes the staleness window before the branch cut') isn't actually true in the one case a prior same-day run already exists, and that the fix belongs in the reuse path reconciling with the freshly-confirmed `main`, not in reverting the reuse behavior itself — matching that direction kept both item 4's and item 5's original design rationales intact instead of re-litigating either. Merge-over-rebase and stop-on-conflict-rather-than-resolve were both judgment calls not dictated by the review comment itself, so recorded here per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule rather than left only in this commit's diff.

checklist.step: `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section (steps 1-4) doesn't instruct getting a real current timestamp via `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` before writing the `decisions`/`questions` entry it appends when reopening a task — unlike `pr-reviewer`'s own instructions, which explicitly call this out. This project has a documented failure mode (MEMORY.md's 'Orchestrator merge-ordering failure' note) where a guessed/estimated timestamp breaks downstream ordering checks (e.g. `pr_decision.confirmed_at` vs `review.reviewed_at`). Add the same explicit 'always get the real current time via `date -u`, never estimate' instruction to this skill's flagging steps.

`.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section doesn't address what to do with a reopened task's existing `review`/`pr_decision` fields (which still say `verdict: "accepted"` / `verdict: "merge"` after the task is reverted to `implementing`/`waiting_input`). Leaving them as-is could mislead a future reader/agent into thinking the task was genuinely re-confirmed as accepted after being reopened. Clarify the intended handling (e.g. explicitly note in the skill that these are left as a historical record of the prior review cycle, to be naturally superseded once the task goes through `pr-reviewer`/`pr-decision` again — or have the skill annotate them) so it isn't ambiguous.

`.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` invites 'periodic/scheduled' invocation (per its own description) but neither the skill file nor CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time on the shared working tree' coordination rule (which currently names task-worker/pr-reviewer/pr-decision/pr-merger explicitly) accounts for this skill running while one of those is mid-flight on the same checkout — its git mv / index.json edits could intermix with an in-flight agent's uncommitted changes. Add an explicit caveat to the skill (and/or extend CLAUDE.md's coordination rule to include this skill) once the blocking persistence/staleness fixes from the parent task's own checklist land. Partially mitigated by SKILL.md's new step 0 (added for the blocking staleness fix), which now tells the invoker to run `git status` first and abort if another agent looks mid-flight — but the residual gap remains open: (a) it only catches an agent that has already made an uncommitted change, not one that's merely reading/running tests mid-flight with a clean tree, and (b) CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time' rule still doesn't name `revalidate-done-tasks` in its list of coordinating agents/skills. Close this out only once one of those two residual gaps is actually addressed.

Re-review (PR #92) via the `code-review` skill: the audit branch name `audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>` (SKILL.md 'Handling a task that no longer holds', step 1) has no disambiguator for a second run on the same calendar day — `git switch -c` collides and aborts the run if the skill is invoked twice in one day (e.g. a manual rerun while an earlier day's PR is still open, or a sub-daily schedule cadence via the `schedule` skill). Add a fallback (branch-name suffix, or reuse/append to the existing same-day branch).

Re-review (PR #92) via the `code-review` skill: step 0's up-to-date-`main` checkout happens once before the (potentially multi-minute) full backend+frontend suite run in step 3, but 'Handling a task that no longer holds' step 1 cuts the audit branch afterward 'from an up-to-date main (per step 0 above)' without re-fetching — so if another agent's PR merges to `main` while the suites are running, the audit branch (and the PR opened from it) is based on a `main` ref that's already gone stale by the time it's cut, missing the intervening commit(s). A skill whose whole purpose is catching staleness elsewhere has a small residual staleness window in its own mechanics. Consider re-confirming `main` is still current immediately before cutting the branch, not just at step 0.

Blocking finding from PR #93's `code-review` re-review: the item-4 fix (same-day branch-collision handling, step 1 of 'Handling a task that no longer holds') and the item-5 fix (re-confirm/pull `main` immediately before cutting the branch) don't compose. When the collision-handling path reuses an existing open-PR same-day branch (`git fetch origin <branch> && git switch <branch>`), that branch is NOT re-cut from the freshly re-confirmed `main` — it's whatever `main` it was originally cut from, potentially many commits behind by the time a later same-day run adds findings to it. This silently reintroduces the exact staleness gap item 5 was written to close, just relocated to the branch-reuse path instead of being eliminated. Fix by having the reuse path also rebase/merge the freshly-confirmed `main` into the reused branch (or otherwise reconcile the two), and note in the eventual PR body if that rebase/merge picked up new commits.

comments.summary: BLOCKING (surfaced by the `code-review` skill's fuller pass, which returned after my initial manual-review-only accept had already been posted — this entry supersedes that accept): the item-4 fix (same-day branch-collision handling) and the item-5 fix (re-confirm/pull `main` immediately before cutting the branch) don't compose. On the collision path that reuses an existing open-PR same-day branch (`git fetch origin <branch> && git switch <branch>`), that branch is NOT re-cut from the freshly re-confirmed `main` from the step-1 fetch/pull moments earlier — it's still based on whatever `main` it was originally cut from, which may now be many commits behind. This silently reintroduces the exact staleness gap item 5 was written to close, just relocated to the branch-reuse path rather than eliminated — meaning item 5's checklist claim ('closes the staleness window before the branch cut') isn't actually true in the one case (same-day rerun) where a prior run already exists. Needs the reuse path to also reconcile the reused branch with the freshly-confirmed `main` (rebase/merge), and to note in the PR body if that picked up new commits.

All five originally-listed checklist items were independently verified as textually present and accurate against the actual current SKILL.md/CLAUDE.md content — that part of the review stands. Tests/coverage/lint were run and are unaffected (docs-only diff): backend pytest-cov 99.84%, frontend vitest --coverage ~99.7%, eslint/tsc clean, ruff/mypy correctly not configured/invoked. No API/schema, frontend-component, signals/portfolio, or new-module change, so those checks don't apply; no UI surface, so the browser walkthrough is explicitly skipped.

Non-blocking (nit): SKILL.md 'Handling a task that no longer holds' step 1's same-day branch-collision text is self-contradictory — "the name is free to reuse for a new, unrelated run — fall back to a numeric-suffixed name instead" says both that the name is free to reuse and, in the same breath, that it should not be reused but suffixed instead. Tracked on the `skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups-followups` follow-up task (not blocking on its own).

Non-blocking: the same-day audit-branch collision handling doesn't say what to do if a same-named branch exists (locally or on origin) with no PR at all, e.g. a prior run that cut the branch but crashed before pushing/opening a PR. Tracked on the `skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups-followups` follow-up task (not blocking on its own).

review.notes: Correction to my own earlier pass on this PR: I initially posted an accept after a manual line-by-line read plus running tests/coverage/lint, having launched the `code-review` skill in the background but not yet having its result. That background run subsequently returned a third finding (the item-4/item-5 composition bug above) that I'd missed manually and that is genuinely blocking, not a wording nit like the other two it (and I) found — it means one of this PR's own three claimed fixes doesn't actually hold in the specific case (same-day rerun with an already-open PR) it was supposed to cover. Reverting the task to `implementing` and the file to `docs/tasks/` (out of `done/`) per the needs_work path; added the composition bug as a new checklist item (item 6) on this task so the next `task-worker` pass has the exact failure scenario and fix direction rather than having to re-derive it. The two non-blocking wording/edge-case findings remain tracked on `skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups-followups` and don't need to move. No stale `pr_decision` existed on this task to clear.
